chunks: From him, from his father, from Hariz, from Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Verily, when Allah, the Exalted and Glorious, created Adam (peace be upon him), He breathed into him from His spirit, so he moved before the spirit was fully blown into him.' He said: 'Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: O Adam, where are you going?' He said: 'I ask You by the right of Muhammad and his Family that You blow into me from Your spirit.' He said: 'So He blew into him from His spirit.' He said: 'Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: O Adam, rise and prostrate to the angels.' He said: 'He said: O Lord, for what reason?' He said: 'Because I created you with My hand.' He said: 'He said: O Lord, for I have created the angels from My light.' He said: 'He said: I have commanded you, so prostrate.' He said: 'So he prostrated.' He said: 'Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: O Adam, it is not for you to ask Me by the right of Muhammad and his Family except for what you have asked.' He said: 'He said: O Lord, protect me from the evil of Satan.' He said: 'He said: It is not for you to ask Me by the right of Muhammad and his Family except for what you have asked.'
ai.seo_question: What did Adam ask for by the right of Muhammad and his Family during his creation?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq presents this narration to establish the pre-existence and cosmic authority of the Ahl al-Bayt, arguing that their 'right' (Haqq) was the medium through which Adam secured divine mercy and protection from Satan. This highlights the Shia theological principle that the Prophet and his Family are the intercessors and the means of closeness to Allah, a concept rooted in the very creation of the first human. The story serves as a foundational proof for the spiritual superiority of the Imams, linking Adam's plea directly to the light of Muhammad and Ali.
